glance_takeaway: This is a post-incident analysis (INC-1194, SEV-1) of a 4-hour-17-minute partial outage of a 'Ledgerline Invoicing API' on June 24, 2026, drawn as a river-basin metaphor. The main message is that there was no single root cause: a bad deploy (a search rewritten to a leading-wildcard LIKE that couldn't use an index) was the trigger, but two pre-existing weaknesses — a 'silted' database (dead tuples from a backfill) and jitterless fixed-interval retries — amplified one endpoint's regression into a valley-wide outage saturating a shared pgbouncer pool, with 68 minutes lost to a wrong diagnosis. Key numbers a reader absorbs: 31.2% peak error rate, 2,312 orgs affected (24.4%), ~$41,300 in SLA credits, zero data loss, and 3 P0 fixes targeted for Q3 2026, one per contributing factor.

F1.note: Header eyebrow '2026-06-24, 14:02–18:19 UTC' + 'SEV-1'; KPI chip '4 h 17 m outage'; flow log '257 min'.

F2.note: Damage survey: '19.1% average across the window; peak 31.2% at 15:47'; '≈362,000 of ≈1.9 M requests'.

F3.note: Damage survey: 'p50 85 ms → 2.9 s; p99 420 ms → 28.4 s' + note that 504s at 30 s count as errors, not latency.

F4.note: Customer districts panel + damage survey: 2,312 orgs (24.4% of 9,480), ≈$41,300 across 216 enterprise contracts, zero data loss, 37,400 webhooks all replayed by 19:05.

F5.note: Section 1: PR #8841 leading-wildcard LIKE, org scoping moved to app-side, cost 0.56..8.44 → 0.00..6,214,891, 0.4 ms → 24–31 s, 'Rows Removed by Filter: 312,344,806', 274.2 M-row table.

F6.note: Section 1 'Why canary didn't catch it': ~2 M rows, same seq scan ~180 ms, under every threshold.

F7.note: Section 2: Jun 22 backfill of 38.1 M rows, 38.1 M dead tuples, 12.2% bloat, heap 190→213 GB, 20% scale factor → ≈54.9 M threshold never crossed.

F8.note: Section 2: ~26 s bloat-free estimate → 24–31 s straddling the 30-s levee; ~57% killed (query_canceled) as 5xx; killed query still held its connection the full 30 s.

F9.note: Section 4: 80-connection pgbouncer pool shared by reads/writes/PDF/webhooks; ≈5.6/s retry-multiplied arrivals → ≈160+ demand; saturated 15:12; cl_waiting peak 1,437 at 15:58; 'the blast radius stopped being search'.

F10.note: Section 3 + timeline: fixed 1 s, 3 attempts, no jitter, no budget; 3,200 → 15,020 rpm (4.7×); zero extra successes; pool pinned 15:12–17:18; pool bump 80→200 at 16:20 worsened write latency, reverted 16:31.

F11.note: Section 5 + timeline: network hypothesis 14:20–15:10 (50 min), anchored by 14:05 cloud advisory + gateway 504s + deploy markers broken since Jun 10; 68 min from 14:11 alert to 15:19 diagnosis.

F12.note: Section 6: migration 0412 dropped idx_invoices_org_number; code rollback would still seq-scan; rebuild ~6 h; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY 16:05 → 21:48, after incident close.

F13.note: Section 6 + timeline: invoice_search_contains set to 0% at 17:05 after 16:35 staging verification of the exact-match fallback on the untouched unique index; <3% by 17:15; flip took 90 s; re-enabled June 26.

F14.note: Section 6 + timeline: manual VACUUM (ANALYZE) 17:12–17:50 removing 38.1 M dead tuples and refreshing stats; SLOs met from 17:53; closed 18:19 after 26 min stable.

F15.note: Section 5: only firing alert was gateway 5xx > 2%/5 min at 14:11; no latency SLO alert for invoicing despite p99 exploding 14:07; 1/100 sampling (~0.7 samples/min); broken deploy marker hid the 14:02 deploy from every graph.

F16.note: Flood-defenses table: 9 items, 3×P0/3×P1/3×P2, named owners and target quarters; P0s (Q3 2026) = latency SLO alerts (Priya N.), pgbouncer saturation alerting + isolation (Marcus T.), standardized retries with backoff/jitter/budgets (Dana K.); P1s include migration-reversibility policy, autovacuum tuning, CI query-plan checks.

strengths: Perfect fact coverage: all 16 key facts are on the page, numerically exact, most in two reinforcing places (map annotation + prose/table).
The causal structure (trigger + two amplifiers) is the page's literal geography, and the 'no storm / no silt / no pump storm' counterfactual panel makes T1 explicit rather than implied.
Unusually honest: a 'Where the metaphor breaks' section pre-empts the three ways the river analogy would mislead, plus 'Notes on the numbers' caveats and retrospective markers in the timeline.
DB mechanisms (dead tuples, covering index, pgbouncer) each get an explicit one-line 'Gloss:' — exactly what the brief's non-DB-specialist audience needs.
Layered structure for re-finding: KPI chips, numbered map keyed to sections, proportional 257-min flow bar, full timeline table, damage-survey table, owner/quarter remediation table.
weaknesses: The rollback-impossible / feature-flag-saved-the-day takeaway (T3) does not land at a glance — 'old bypass' and 'sluice gate' are small, metaphor-coded map labels that only pay off after reading the legend.
Metaphor-first section headings ('The wrong valley', 'The bypass that couldn't be re-dug') tax scanning: a reader hunting for 'rollback' or 'detection' must translate through the analogy.
The map's center is busy: small annotation text, a dashed retry loop crossing other labels, and dense multi-line callouts reduce legibility at the illustration's core.
The page is very long (~10k px); the brief's 'few minutes' reading goal is met only if the reader trusts the layering and skips, and the blameless framing appears only below the fold.
River widths and flooded areas are illustrative, not quantitative encodings — honest here because annotated, but the visual channel itself carries no measured data outside the flow bar.
evaluator_notes: Accuracy is mechanical: 16/16 conveyed, 0 distorted, 0 contradicted -> 10 x 16/16 = 10.0. Glance (scored strictly from the recorded takeaway): T1 fully landed, T2 headline only, T4 mostly, T3 absent -> 7.0. Overall = 0.35*10.0 + 0.30*7.0 + 0.15*8.0 + 0.10*7.5 + 0.10*7.5 = 3.5 + 2.1 + 1.2 + 0.75 + 0.75 = 8.3. Caveat fidelity is true and exceptional (metaphor-break section, estimate hedges, 'reusable not returned' disk note, 'affected' definition). Blameless tone of the source is preserved ('systems, tools, and process gaps — not people'). Rendering intact in both screenshots; page notes horizontal scroll on narrow screens but desktop capture is clean. Depth held below 8.5 because the metaphor indirection adds real translation overhead for a first-time reader despite the legend; structure and craft held at 7.5 for the metaphor-coded headings and the crowded map center.
